title: Custom platform paid only on acceptance

company.company_business: IT implementation and managed services for mid-size Indian businesses

narrative_template:
Kalmira is building a custom claims platform for {customer} on Kalmira's own development servers. The design is so specific to the customer that it could not be sold to anyone else without major rework. The customer pays only when it accepts the finished platform; if it cancels before then, it owes nothing for the work done.

Is revenue recognised over time or at a point in time? If over time, which paragraph 35 criterion is met?

Round amounts to the nearest rupee and percentages to one decimal place. All names are fictional.

rubric.text: At a point in time: 35(c) fails without a right to payment for work to date.

model_answer_template: At a point in time, on acceptance.
explanation: If no paragraph 35 criterion is met, the obligation is satisfied at a point in time, when the customer obtains control (para 38). Without a right to payment for work to date, 35(c) fails.

mistakes.feedback: No alternative use is met, but 35(c) also needs an enforceable right to payment for work completed to date (para 37). Payment only on acceptance fails that, so revenue is recognised when control passes at acceptance (para 38).
The customer does not control the platform while it is built on Kalmira's servers, so 35(b) fails.
The customer gets nothing until acceptance, so 35(a) fails.
